name: Fenris Ballistics Howl FB-7 'Wolfpack'
description:
A precision rifle that fires programmable micro-munitions capable of splitting into three independently-guided sub-projectiles after leaving the barrel. Each sub-projectile carries its own BCI-slaved guidance package and can engage a separate target within a 15-degree cone from the initial trajectory.

Fenris Ballistics designed the Howl for scenarios where a single sniper needs to engage multiple targets simultaneously — a capability previously requiring multiple shooters. The weapon's split-munition technology uses explosive bolt separation at a pre-programmed range, after which each sub-projectile follows its own BCI-designated target lock.

The Wolfpack's limitation is that the sub-projectiles carry significantly less kinetic energy than a full-size round. Against armored targets, the split munitions may fail to penetrate. Against unarmored or lightly armored personnel, three simultaneous hits from unexpected angles produce devastating psychological and physical effect.
legality: Licensed — military and corporate tactical teams
specifications: caliber: 8mm parent munition splitting to 3x 4mm sub-projectiles effective_range: 100-1,200 meters (split at 50-800m operator-selected) rate_of_fire: 1 round per 3 seconds capacity: 6-round detachable magazine weight: 7.2 kg power_source: BCI guidance link, no external power required
tactical_use: The Wolfpack excels in multi-target engagement scenarios — ambush interdiction, convoy disruption, and security detail neutralization. A single Howl operator can engage a three-person bodyguard detail simultaneously, eliminating the sequential engagement delay that gives targets time to react. The weapon is also used for guaranteed kills, with all three sub-projectiles directed at a single target for redundant lethality.
cultural_context: Fenris Ballistics takes its name and branding from Norse predator mythology, and the Wolfpack embodies their philosophy of overwhelming the prey. The weapon has found particular favor with corporate extraction teams who need to neutralize protective details quickly and cleanly. Among close protection professionals, the Wolfpack is the weapon they fear most — three rounds from three angles, and no time to react.
story_hooks: A Wolfpack round split into its sub-projectiles and two of the three guidance packages locked onto unintended targets — bystanders who happened to match the biometric profile of the intended victims. Fenris claims this is impossible with properly calibrated BCI targeting.

Someone has reverse-engineered the split-munition technology and is manufacturing bootleg copies with unreliable separation charges. Three operators have been killed when the parent munition detonated inside the barrel.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular precision rifle with a pronounced bullpup-influenced silhouette. The receiver tapers from a robust breech assembly to a slender, almost surgical barrel. The overall aesthetic is predatory—sharp lines and minimal ornamentation. The gun reads as purpose-built military hardware, with an almost organic aggression to its form.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 98 cm | Barrel length: 61 cm | Width at receiver: 8.5 cm | Height with scope rail: 12 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but well-balanced. At 7.2 kg, it settles into the shoulder with confident authority—substantial enough to absorb recoil, but not so heavy as to feel unwieldy during sustained aim.
physical_description.primary_material: Titanium-reinforced polymer chassis with steel receiver and barrel. The breach housing shows machined steel to handle the explosive bolt separation mechanism.
physical_description.finish: Deep matte charcoal polymer with brushed steel accents around the receiver and breech. High-wear areas show a silvered burnish from repeated handling. The barrel has a faint oil-slick iridescence from bore coating.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte charcoal-black primary with gunmetal gray steel accents. Subtle teal accent lines run along the rail system—BCI-linked status indicators.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with shallow fingergrooves. Slightly tacky rubberized overmold for secure purchase even in gloved hands. The magazine well is reinforced with slight ribbing.
distinctive_features: Flush-mounted BCI interface pad on the left receiver—pale luminescent ring that pulses when linked to guidance package
Three precision-machined apertures visible at the muzzle brake, hinting at the internal separation mechanism
Elongated charging handle set slightly proud of the body for tactical glove compatibility
Magazine marked with trio of red diamond symbols indicating split-munition loadout
Integrated rail system with low-profile mounting points for optics—designed for minimal profile
Heat vents along the receiver body, barely visible but tactilely apparent
Serial plate on left side reads: FENRIS FB-7-WOLFPACK with micro-etched batch codes
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: FENRIS BALLISTICS stamped in small caps on the left receiver. A raised Fenris wolf-head logo (stylized single eye) embossed on the magazine floorplate. Serial designation plate inset flush into the lower receiver with batch traceability codes.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but maintained. Polymer shows micro-scratches and slight discoloration from weather exposure. Steel components retain luster but show faint patina from regular use. No visible damage—this is a weapon that sees regular deployment and professional care.
